title: Sanga (Palm-Nut Soup with Kale and Sweetcorn)
author: Ngwafu Tansie (The Vegan Society)
desc: A UK vegan adaptation: onion and garlic fried in oil, palm-nut cream and water simmered, then kale and sweetcorn added, served with basmati rice.
longDesc: The Vegan Society’s page describes sanga as a popular Cameroonian dish, more specifically within the southern and central regions, traditionally made with cassava leaves, palm oil and maize; this version substitutes kale for the cassava leaves and uses palm-nut cream as the base. Blended onion and garlic are fried in hot oil over medium-high heat, the palm-nut cream added and fried a few minutes, then the water, covered until boiling and then uncovered and simmered about 20 minutes. Kale and salt simmer about 20 minutes and sweetcorn another 5. The rice is cooked 13 minutes without lifting the lid and rested 10.
steps: Blend the onion and garlic and fry in the hot oil over medium-high heat.
Add the palm-nut cream and fry a few minutes.
Add the water, cover until boiling, then uncover and simmer about 20 minutes.
Add the kale and salt and simmer about 20 minutes.
Add the sweetcorn and simmer about 5 minutes more.
Cook the rice 13 minutes without lifting the lid, then rest 10 minutes. Serve together.
chefTips: The page gives times only, no doneness cues.
Do not lift the lid during the rice cooking.
This is a UK adaptation: kale replaces the traditional cassava leaves.
commonMistakes: Lifting the lid on the rice.
Frying the palm-nut cream too long.
Expecting the flavour of the cassava-leaf original.
healthBenefits: Kale and sweetcorn make this a vegetable-heavy dish; palm-nut cream is high in fat.
culturalNote: The page says sanga is popular in the southern and central regions and traditionally made with cassava leaves, palm oil and maize. A second Afrik printing (Amina Savoura, 27 June 2017) describes the Central African original with black nightshade (zom) and fresh maize but prints no quantities.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Sanga (palm nut soup, Mbanga)’. Credit as printed: ‘Recipe written and created by Ngwafu Tansie’ (The Vegan Society). No date printed (flagged). Serves 6 and 6 (rice). Prep 10 min, cook 42 min, total 52 min as printed. Ingredients TWO-PASS; method SINGLE-PASS.

As printed, not fixed: ‘Allow to simmer in the pot for a 20 minutes’ (typo); the step times (20 + 20 + 5) do not obviously add to the 42-minute figure. This is a vegan adaptation, not a traditional mbanga.
